body:
### Ⅰ. Motivation

The plugin ecosystem growing around community inference engines (SGLang, vLLM) needs a way to place its artifacts — acceleration packs, interposition libraries, C++ hooks — into rendering workloads. The plugin publisher cannot write the user's workload; the workload author does not know the plugin's internals. [issue #531](https://github.com/sgl-project/rbg/issues/531) inventories the gaps in the current injection mechanism:

1. Pod-level injection is unscoped — a role cannot say "this runtime belongs to the worker component".
2. A profile cannot touch role-declared containers — no second delivery dimension exists.
3. Role-side customization of profile containers is env/args-only, expressed as full `corev1.Container` objects with extra fields silently ignored.

This PR adds the KEP-531 design document.

### Ⅱ. Modifications

New `keps/531-engine-runtime-profile-injection/` (README.md + kep.yaml). Design highlights:

- **`component`** (optional) on an `engineRuntimes` reference scopes it to exactly one component of the role's pattern; absent = main's default component set (leader-only under leaderWorkerPattern), byte-for-byte compatible with existing references. Scope ownership forbids two component-scoped references to the same (profile, component); render-time validation is the authoritative gate, CEL checks shape only.
- **`targetContainers`** (optional) is the per-container consent line: one entry per container the reference touches, keyed by `name` (duplicates rejected by `+listType=map`). Listing a **role-declared** name is consent for the profile's `containerPatches` to fire there; the entry's `extraPatches` carry the role's own rules for the same container, landing after the profile's. Entries naming **profile-declared** containers receive only their own `extraPatches` — the profile's rules are written for the consumer's engine containers, never for its own — and are the forward-compat channel for the day `containerPatches` replaces the legacy `containers` merge.
- **Patch grammar**: a shared RFC 6902 add-only grammar with five allowlisted roots (env, command, args, volumeMounts, Linux capabilities). The root allowlist is side-asymmetric — the profile side may only address the shape-independent roots (env, volumeMounts, the outermost `/command/0` wrap), while argv surgery and capabilities are role-side-only, because only the role author knows the container's command/args shape. Patches land verbatim at their stated positions — no render-time winner rule; same-name env entries resolve by their own positions (kubelet last-occurrence semantics), with a warning event (`EngineRuntimeEnvCollision`) on cross-source collisions.
- **Profile immutability**: a referenced profile's spec is frozen and deletion pends on an in-use finalizer (PVC-protection shape) — a revision ships as a new profile and consumers migrate references one at a time, each migration an explicit re-consent. Enforcement is a CERP validating webhook staged alpha-warning / beta-rejection (`failurePolicy: Fail`), consulting references across RoleBasedGroups and RoleBasedGroupSets cluster-wide via an uncached lookup; the controller's CERP watch emits a warning event on any spec change that slips past a failed or uninstalled webhook. `--disable-profile-immutability` (alpha-only) is the escape hatch that turns the freeze and finalizer off without rolling back the image. `updateStrategy` is deprecated — it was never consumed, and immutability removes the surface it would have governed.
- **RoleBasedGroupSet propagation**: no second implementation — group-template roles carry `component`/`targetContainers` deep-copied into each child RBG and render with identical semantics; role-side invariants are rejected at write time by the RBGSet webhook.
- **Compatibility**: four write-time scenarios; pre-existing references render byte-for-byte identically to main; the legacy `containers` merge keeps its exact outcome; the inert `injectContainers` and the deprecated `updateStrategy` are removed at the next version boundary. The one deliberate write-path change: with the new controller running, spec edits to — and deletion of — referenced profiles are flagged (alpha) / rejected (beta).

### Ⅲ. Does this pull request fix one issue?

Refs #531 (design doc; implementation will follow in separate PRs).

### Ⅳ. List of the added test cases (unit test/integration test) if any, please explain if no tests are needed.

None — documentation-only PR (KEP design). The KEP's Test Plan section specifies the unit/envtest/e2e matrix for the follow-up implementation.

### Ⅴ. Describe how to verify it

Review the KEP document: `keps/531-engine-runtime-profile-injection/README.md`.

### VI. Special notes for reviews

The design went through several revisions during review: consolidation of the consent list and the role's own rules into a single `targetContainers` entry per container (with `extraPatches`, replacing the earlier `patchContainers` model), the side-asymmetric root allowlist, the leader-only default-component correction against the actual reconciler code, patch-pass ordering with role-side patches last and verbatim positional env landing (no render-time normalization), and the profile-immutability redesign (freeze while referenced, in-use finalizer, staged webhook enforcement, controller watch backstop, `--disable-profile-immutability` escape hatch, `updateStrategy` deprecation). The Compatibility Guarantees section and the Test Plan's byte-for-byte upgrade tests are the surface to scrutinize.
